question: In a group of 60 students, 38 study Mathematics, 32 study Physics and 18 study both subjects. If a student selected at random is known to study at least one of the two subjects, determine the conditional probability that the selected student studies exactly one of the two subjects.
explanation:
Given Information
Let $M$ denote the event that a student studies Mathematics and $P$ denote the event that a student studies Physics. We have $n(M)=38$, $n(P)=32$ and $n(M\cap P)=18$.

The condition that the student studies at least one subject corresponds to $M\cup P$. Therefore,
$$n(M\cup P)=n(M)+n(P)-n(M\cap P)=38+32-18=52.$$

The number of students studying Mathematics only is
$$38-18=20,$$
and the number studying Physics only is
$$32-18=14.$$
Hence the number studying exactly one of the two subjects is
$$20+14=34.$$

Let $E$ denote the event that the selected student studies exactly one subject and let $F=M\cup P$. Since every outcome in $E$ is also in $F$, $E\cap F=E$. Thus,
$$P(E\cap F)=\frac{34}{60},\qquad P(F)=\frac{52}{60}.$$
Using conditional probability,
$$P(E|F)=\frac{P(E\cap F)}{P(F)}=\frac{\frac{34}{60}}{\frac{52}{60}}=\frac{34}{52}=\frac{17}{26}.$$

Final Result
Therefore, the conditional probability that the selected student studies exactly one of the two subjects is $\frac{17}{26}$.
